claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your Child Benefit eligibility! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question.

**How old is the child (or children) you'd like to check eligibility for?**

Please let me know:
- The child's name and date of birth (or current age)
- If you have multiple children, I'll assess each one

The age of the child is important because:
- **Under 16**: Children automatically qualify (assuming other criteria are met)
- **16-19**: Children need to be in qualifying education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible for Child Benefit

Please provide the child's age or date of birth so I can continue the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh hi, yes I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I've got one child - Alex, who's 9 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 9 years old, which means he falls into the **under 16** category and is a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me proceed with the next checks to determine your eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is only 9 years old, I expect this will be straightforward - but I need to confirm for our assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just at primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected at age 9. Alex is not working, so he passes this check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Again, at age 9 this is unlikely, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name - he's only 9!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT in any kind of apprenticeship?**

Again, at age 9, I expect he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's far too young for that!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now we need to check the eligibility criteria for **you** as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now let's check your residency eligibility. Do any of the following apply to you?**

**Path 1 - Normally resident in the UK:**
- You normally live in the UK

**Path 2 - EU Settlement Scheme (Settled Status):**
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

**Path 3 - EU Settlement Scheme (Pre-settled + Working):**
- You have pre-settled status AND
- You're working and earning (or expect to earn) above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months

**Path 4 - EU Settlement Scheme (Pre-settled + Job Seeking):**
- You have pre-settled status AND
- You're actively looking for work (can claim for up to 91 days)

**Path 5 - EU Settlement Scheme (Pre-settled + Sufficient Resources):**
- You have pre-settled status AND
- You have sufficient financial resources to support yourself and your family AND
- You're NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit

**Path 6 - EU Settlement Scheme (Pre-settled + Studying):**
- You have pre-settled status AND
- You're studying with sufficient resources to support yourself

**Path 7 - EU Settlement Scheme (Pre-settled + Family Member):**
- You have pre-settled status AND
- You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with a right to reside AND
- You're their spouse/civil partner, dependent child/grandchild under 21, or dependent parent/grandparent

**Path 8 - Crown Servant Abroad:**
- You're living abroad as a Crown servant in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these, if any, applies to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirements as you normally live in the UK. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next, I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. Do any of the following apply?**

**Path 1 - Living with the child:**
- You live with Alex

**Path 2 - Contributing to the child's upkeep:**
- You pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's care
- This includes contributions towards: food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents
- Can be weekly, monthly, or lump sum payments

**Path 3 - Maintenance payments:**
- You make maintenance payments to Alex under a court order or formal agreement
- These payments cover Alex's upkeep and equal or exceed the Child Benefit payment

**Which of these applies to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- A grandparent or other relative
- Any other person

Please let me know the situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me proceed with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where does Alex currently live?**

- **In hospital:** Is Alex currently in hospital?
- **In care:** Is Alex in care (residential care home, secure accommodation, etc.)?
- **Fostered:** Is Alex fostered by you or someone else?
- **Normal living:** Does Alex live at home normally (as you mentioned)?

I expect the answer is "normal living," but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home normally with me, yes.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives at home with you normally. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- The council is not funding Alex's care, accommodation, or upkeep
- You are responsible for supporting Alex financially

Please confirm this for the final step of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm the one looking after him and paying for everything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You've passed all the eligibility checks. Based on the assessment, you are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me now provide your final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit

**For: Alex (age 9)**

---

### Summary of Your Eligibility

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex:

✓ **Alex's requirements:**
- Age 9 (under 16 - automatic qualifying age)
- Not working more than 24 hours per week
- Not receiving benefits in his own right
- Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- Living at home with you normally

✓ **Your (claimant) requirements:**
- You live in the UK (Manchester) - residency requirement met
- You live with Alex - responsibility requirement met
- No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council is not funding Alex's care

---

### Next Steps

You can now proceed to **claim Child Benefit**:

1. **Online at:** [www.gov.uk/apply-child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/apply-child-benefit)
2. **By phone:** Call the Child Benefit Office on **0300 200 3100**
3. **By post:** Complete form CH2 and send it to the Child Benefit Office

When you claim, you'll need:
- Your National Insurance number
- Alex's full name and date of birth
- Details about your income (if applicable)
- Bank account details for payments

---

Congratulations! You should receive Child Benefit payments for Alex. If you have any further questions, feel free to contact HMRC or visit the official Child Benefit guidance page.
